title: Phase design spec document structure
description: Canonical structure of an osuperpowers phase design spec — one phase's increment of a program; the program-level charter lives in the parent overall (whole-program conventions win on conflict). This schema is the single structure fact for the phase-spec doc type: the artifact header block, the fixed Section 0–5 skeleton (skeleton isomorphism — do not insert sections mid-sequence, each number is one semantic), the unique `### Acceptance criteria` subsection inside Section 2, and the deviations table whose `Overall updated?` column must be `Yes` before review. Authoring agents read the properties + descriptions to draft conforming specs; docContractValidate consumes the same patterns (`**Version**` strictly required, Class-B parent-program lineage).

header.description: Artifact header block — metadata at the top of the artifact, a bullet block, not a `##` section. The `**Version**` line is STRICTLY required here (the phase-spec Version check); every remaining field is part of the block.

marker.description: The canonical `**Version**` marker (shared token with the overall; the engine derives its phase-spec version assertion from the same single source).

line.description: The strictly-required version line; the `v\d+\.\d+` token follows the version-lineage rule (must reference a version the parent overall actually carries when the spec pins one).

states.description: Phase-spec status states — Draft / Approved / Plan pending / Shipped.

author.description: `**Author**` — contributor line (`[human] · [harness + model]`); free text, no structural rule.

parentProgram.description: `**Parent program**` — link + version to the parent overall; Class-B lineage check resolves it to an existing `*-overall.md` and requires every `vX.Y` token on the line to be in the parent's lineage (current `**Version:**` ∪ change-history cells).

linkForm.description: `- **Parent program**: [<name>-overall.md vX.Y](<path>)` — markdown link to the parent overall doc (`*-overall.md`).

dependsOn.description: `**Depends on**` — upstream phases + tags (e.g. `P1（shipped · [p1-design v1.1](…)）`; informational.

sections.description: The fixed Section 0–5 skeleton — Section 0–5 artifact body, each number one semantic, fixed order (skeleton isomorphism — no mid-sequence insertion; the 'Section N' labels belong to the family skeleton, each artifact section is authored under its literal `## Section N: <name>` heading).

section0.description: Section 0 — Incremental warning: the spec commits to exactly one phase; splitting / reordering a phase's work is not a local edit — phase-inventory rows, dependency edges and a change-history row land in the parent overall first (backfill-as-version).

section1.description: Section 1 — Constraints pointer: does not repeat overall conventions; cross-phase rules belong in the overall (overall wins on conflict).

section2.description: Section 2 — Design body: this phase's increment (approaches, architecture, components, data flow, errors, testing) AND the `### Acceptance criteria` subsection (see acceptanceCriteria).

section3.description: Section 3 — Deviations from overall: the deviations table (`Overall assumption | Phase decision | Overall updated?`); required when the phase diverges on a cross-phase matter.

heading.description: Literal heading `## Section 3: Deviations from overall`.

columns.description: Three deviation-table columns; `Overall updated?` must be `Yes` (with version + date, e.g. `Yes — vX.Y · YYYY-MM-DD`) before review — a divergence not fed back to the overall is a backfill violation.

section4.description: Section 4 — Notes for downstream: later-phase scope shifts; a 'later phases will handle this' note that stays here alone is a dead end — downstream writers read the overall, record the shift in the overall's issue / phase / dependency tables and history, keep the note as a pointer.

heading.description: Literal heading `## Section 4: Notes for downstream`.

section5.description: Section 5 — Review: fresh-subagent review passes before user review and writing-plans — baseline = committed tree, Review Convergence (blocker > 0 → fix all findings → re-review; blocker = 0 → fix all findings → done, no re-review).

acceptanceCriteria.description: `### Acceptance criteria` — the ONLY subsection, and it lives inside Section 2 (Design body): verifiable completion conditions, each independently testable. An acceptance criterion is a claim: a claim that cannot be mechanically verified on the shipped tree is a paper claim.

heading.description: Literal subsection heading `### Acceptance criteria` — unique: no other subsection exists anywhere in the doc.

location.description: Location rule — the subsection sits inside Section 2 (Design body).

parent.description: `### Acceptance criteria` is nested directly under `## Section 2: Design body`.

entry.description: Acceptance entries — `- ` code-span-prefixed bullets, each an independently testable condition (e.g. `- artifact X exists at path Y with property Z`).

language.description: Repo authoring policy applies to the spec prose — specs at docs/osuperpowers/specs/ are internal program docs in the working language (Strategy B), value tokens (phase ids / tags / SHAs / paths) stay locale-neutral.
